thread:
maya: FYI saw SLO burn right after the 22:30 deploy. /generate p95 spiked and token latency jumped. No kv-cache dashboard visible in the console. incident bot posted an alert.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-14T22:30Z for service=runtime started by @maya (canary).

oncall-bot: Pager assigned to @sam for incident INC-1768002345 — high p95 on /generate (SLO 99.9%).

sam: I'm on it. quick summary pls — is this canary-only?

maya: Looks like canary and a small spillover in prod east. Canary p95 2.4s -> 5.8s. overall traffic ~0.8% error/timeout increase for EU customers. No dashboard for kv_cache_hit_rate so I eyeballed logs.

maya: snippet of logs I pulled:
```
[22:31:02] runtime: slot=canary1 instance=rt-23 req=/generate lat=5800ms tokens=42 cache_hit=false
[22:31:03] runtime: slot=canary2 instance=rt-17 req=/generate lat=5600ms tokens=37 cache_hit=false
```

leo: Is this the new kv-prefix caching flag we flipped in the rollout? ff/kv-prefix was enabled in canary. Can we toggle kill-switch? :rotating_light:

irene: I'm checking alert rules. Curious — the alert that fired is `high_latency_generate` but the suppression rule references metric `kv_cache_hit_rate` which doesn't exist (we ship `cache_hit_rate`). looks like metric renaming in the canary build skipped updating the suppression rule.

sam: Ugh, so suppression missed, alerts noisy -> paging the wrong team. Can we kill the flag and/or rollback the canary? Need to reduce customer impact.

maya: I'll toggle the flag now. command: `ld toggle ff/kv-prefix off --env prod-canary --by maya`

maya: toggled ff/kv-prefix -> off :white_check_mark:

irene: Flag off. I'm seeing an initial drop in cache_miss log lines but alerts still firing because alerting system is matching `cache_hit_rate` vs rule expecting `kv_cache_hit_rate`.

leo: If alerts are firing due to name mismatch we should suppress the alert temporarily while we fix rules. Can someone add a short suppression? ops-bot can you mute high_latency_generate for 15m?

ops-bot: Muting alert `high_latency_generate` for 15 minutes as requested by @leo. Reason: noisy during rollback mitigation.

sam: Also, dashboards missing — where's the runbook for kv cache? I can't find it in the runbooks page. If we're muting alerts we must have manual checks in place.

carol: Customer-impact quick note: support thread #7621 reported timeouts for two EU customers and one internal integration. No data exfiltration. Escalated to EM.

maya: Given risk, I'm starting a rollback to previous release build. @deploy-bot rollback --to 2026-03-14T22:15Z --service runtime --confirm

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by @maya to 2026-03-14T22:15Z. Canary rollback complete on canary cluster in 45s. Observability: re-evaluating metrics.

irene: After rollback I see p95 trending back to baseline. cache_hit_rate jumping back to normal. Alerts are calming down.

sam: Thanks. I'm going to liaise with support to update customers. How long before we can unmute alerts?

ops-bot: Alert unmute scheduled in 10 minutes (automatic) unless canceled.

leo: Action items in case we forget: 1) fix alert suppression rule to reference `cache_hit_rate` OR ship proper metric rename in instrumentation. 2) Add kv_cache_hit_rate -> cache_hit_rate alias in metrics ingestion for a grace period. 3) Create dashboard for cache hit/miss and per-region p95 for rollout visibility. 4) Add runbook entry for ff/kv-prefix kill-switch.

maya: Agreed. Also we need to update deploy checklist: ensure any metric renames include alert/runbook updates + validate suppression rules in staging.

carol: Customer impact queued: sent update to affected accounts + support noted minimal impact.

sam: Handoff note — I'm on pager for another 30m, then @leo will take night coverage. Leaving a pinned summary in #oncall-handoffs.

leo: Acknowledge. I'll follow up with infra to add an alias and push the alert fix first thing in the morning.

irene: I'll file the post-incident ticket: P1-1768002345 — telemetry naming caused alert suppression gap during deploy. Will include timeline, commands used, and minimal repro steps.

maya: Thanks all. Temp mitigation: rollback + mute helped. Long-term: better deploy guardrails for metrics + add canary dashboard.

sam: closing the active page in 15m unless we see regressions. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-1768002345 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager reassigned back to rotation.

maya: Postmortem owners: @irene (write), @leo (alerts & dashboards), @maya (deploy checklist). Will sync tomorrow.

carol: Adding support notes to incident ticket.

irene: Filed ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/P1-1768002345 — will assign subtasks.

sam: Good job team. Learned things here.

maya: tl;dr: 22:30 rollout exposed metric rename bug -> suppression rule mismatch -> noisy paging -> toggle flag + rollback -> mitigate -> follow-ups: dashboards, runbook, alert fix.
